correctness.rationale: The exact isometry y=log(x/(1-x)), g=xf, transforms the weighted norm to Lp(rho dy) with rho=e^(-pAy)(1+e^y)^(p(A-B)), and the operator to one-sided indefinite integration. Translation bounds give ||H||<=1/min(A,B), while long plateau functions in the slower exponential tail give equality; strict translation and Minkowski equality rule out norm attainment. The inverse derivative D=H^{-1} is closed with domain weighted W1p. For lambda nonzero, H-lambda=-lambda(D-1/lambda)H. Explicit left/right convolution inverses establish resolvent regions, a one-dimensional kernel and onto range for A<B, and the exact dual annihilator with codimension-one range for A>B. Cutoff Weyl sequences establish non-Fredholm boundary and a high-frequency test establishes nonclosed range at zero. The proof treats all complex spectral values, equality cases, and strict admissibility bounds. The standalone checker passed 181 finite checks, not used as proof of infinite-dimensional claims.

originality.rationale: Belli et al. (arXiv:2606.08600v1, Theorem 1.3 and §§2-5) determine spectrum and norm only on unweighted Lp(0,1). The weighted two-endpoint rates A,B move independently, and the resulting two-parameter sharp norm, phase transition p=gamma+delta+2 and explicit weighted codimension-one annihilator are not mathematical consequences of an unweighted statement alone. Abadias et al. consider a different Cesaro-Hardy integral kernel. Searches identified related general Hardy, Fredholm and weighted analytic-function theories but no directly covering identical two-weight real-variable classification; generic differential exponential dichotomy is acknowledged as antecedent mechanism. Prior unweighted Fredholm classifications do not cover arbitrary Jacobi weights. Residual risk of a general preexisting weighted dichotomy implication is explicitly retained.
residual_risks: A general weighted first-order differential-operator exponential-dichotomy theorem may imply the Fredholm index and range structure without giving the same explicit normalization.
An older or unindexed exact weighted Cesaro norm/spectral result may exist under Hardy-type or logistic-transform terminology.
A few older operator-theory works were accessible only at abstract/intro level; absence of a match was not inferred from that alone.

value.rationale: The Jacobi beta weights constitute the canonical two-endpoint family on (0,1). Their independent powers make the spectral circles and the eigen/residual Fredholm phase adjustable; even at p=2 a small change of the sum of the Jacobi exponents produces a full eigenvalue or residual crescent instead of the unweighted single circle. The theorem provides a complete sharp norm, nonattainment, spectral domain, exact essential spectrum, point/residual classification, indices and explicit range annihilator. This natural structural transition is not a routine reparameterization of unweighted Lp results. The limitations exclude critical weights and other kernels; no broader theorem is asserted.
